comparisons.peer_topic: Long-term debt characteristics and interest rate management
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company issues fixed- and variable-rate debt in various currencies and uses derivatives, primarily interest rate swaps, to manage interest rate and foreign exchange impacts. At December 31, 2024, the weighted-average interest rate for long-term debt was 4.26% on a contractual basis and 4.40% including derivative effects.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Citigroup (C) disclose the weighted-average interest rates for their long-term debt, breaking down the impact of derivative instruments on these rates. BAC reported weighted-average effective interest rates of 3.80% (total), 3.71% (fixed), and 4.45% (floating) at December 31, 2024, explicitly stating these are contractual rates excluding derivative impacts. Similarly, C reported a weighted-average interest rate of 4.26% on a contractual basis (excluding derivatives) and 4.40% including derivative effects. While both companies report contractual versus derivative-adjusted rates, BAC provides a fixed/floating split in its primary rate disclosure, whereas C reports the derivative effect as a single aggregate adjustment to the total rate.

sentences.text: The weighted-average effective interest rates for total long-term debt (excluding senior structured notes), total fixed-rate debt and total floating-rate debt were 3.80 percent, 3.71 percent and 4.45 percent, respectively, at December 31, 2024, and 3.70 percent, 3.55 percent and 5.21 percent, respectively, at December 31, 2023.
The weighted-average rates are the contractual interest rates on the debt and do not reflect the impacts of derivative transactions.

At December 31, 2024, the Company's overall weighted-average interest rate for long-term debt, excluding structured notes accounted for at fair value, was 4.26% on a contractual basis and 4.40% including the effects of derivative contracts.
It uses derivative contracts, primarily interest rate swaps, to effectively convert a portion of its fixed-rate debt to variable-rate debt.

comparisons.peer_topic: Aggregate Weighted Average Interest Rates Post-Hedging
comparisons.peer_summary: After hedging activities, unsecured long-term borrowings had weighted average interest rates of 5.72% (4.39% fixed, 5.82% floating) as of December 2024 and 6.13% (3.44% fixed, 6.27% floating) as of December 2023, excluding fair value option accounts.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose weighted-average interest rates for long-term debt/borrowings, further segmented by fixed and floating components. BAC reported rates of 3.71% for fixed-rate and 4.45% for floating-rate debt at December 31, 2024. GS reported aggregate weighted average interest rates of 5.72%, with 4.39% related to fixed-rate obligations and 5.82% related to floating-rate obligations as of December 2024. Both disclosures exclude borrowings accounted for at fair value under the fair value option, and both provide the same fixed/floating breakdown structure, although GS explicitly notes its rates are 'after hedging activities' for the aggregate, while BAC presents contractual rates separately from derivative impacts.

sentences.text: The weighted-average effective interest rates for total long-term debt (excluding senior structured notes), total fixed-rate debt and total floating-rate debt were 3.80 percent, 3.71 percent and 4.45 percent, respectively, at December 31, 2024, and 3.70 percent, 3.55 percent and 5.21 percent, respectively, at December 31, 2023.
The weighted-average rates are the contractual interest rates on the debt and do not reflect the impacts of derivative transactions.

In the table above, the aggregate amounts of unsecured long-term borrowings had weighted average interest rates of 5.72% (4.39% related to fixed-rate obligations and 5.82% related to floating-rate obligations) as of December 2024 and 6.13% (3.44% related to fixed-rate obligations and 6.27% related to floating-rate obligations) as of December 2023.
These rates exclude unsecured long-term borrowings accounted for at fair value under the fair value option.

comparisons.peer_summary: Weighted-average contractual interest rates were 3.82% in 2024 and 3.65% in 2023; JPMorgan Chase uses interest rate and cross-currency swaps to modify exposure, resulting in modified weighted-average interest rates of 5.15% and 5.20% for the same periods, excluding the effects of associated derivatives from the contractual rate figures.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclose weighted-average contractual interest rates for long-term debt excluding structured notes, and also provide modified rates that include the effects of derivative instruments. BAC reported contractual rates of 3.80% (total) at Dec 31, 2024, while JPM reported 3.82%. Both companies also report modified weighted-average rates including derivatives: JPM reported 5.15% for 2024, while BAC did not provide a single aggregate 'modified' rate in the same sentence but detailed fixed (3.71%) and floating (4.45%) contractual rates, noting its ALM strategy uses derivatives to manage interest rate risk. JPM explicitly states its modified rate includes derivative effects, similar to how BAC separates contractual rates from derivative impacts.

The weighted-average rates are the contractual interest rates on the debt and do not reflect the impacts of derivative transactions.
The weighted-average contractual interest rates for total long-term debt excluding structured notes accounted for at fair value were 3.82% and 3.65% as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The modified weighted-average interest rates for total long-term debt, including the effects of related derivative instruments, were 5.15% and 5.20% as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
